attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own essay, written in his own voice.

semantics.note: 'At some point the momentum behind NVIDIA slows' is a firm statement with no deadline. The 'maybe' that follows hedges only how it happens, not whether. The collapse in the surrounding text is correctly kept out of this claim.

contract.note: Reading 'momentum' to include investor momentum is fair, because the speaker himself says sentiment can weaken without sales slowing. Requiring a sustained interruption rather than a one-day dip is an ordinary reading. The claim is weak but scorable.

evidence.note: Dated 2026-02-27 financial analysis: shares had been in a trading range since November 2025. That is a multi-month interruption of upward share-price momentum after publication.
NVIDIA filing: revenue was still growing strongly in mid-2026. This rules out a commercial slowdown but does not touch the investor-momentum branch.

reviews.rationale: There is no deadline, but the contract's early-resolution rule is met: a dated record (e1) shows NVIDIA shares stuck in a range for about four months, from November 2025 to February 2026, after publication. Revenue kept growing (e2), so only the investor-momentum branch is satisfied, which the speaker's own context allows. Later recovery does not undo it.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own essay.

semantics.note: A dependence claim: NVIDIA's value needs sales to grow every quarter. Reading 'value' into 'relies' is reasonable given the stock-value discussion just before it.

contract.note: The contract demands comprehensive GPU unit data and rules out revenue. But the speaker's own framing is revenue growth ('I am keeping this simple'). Insisting on units, which NVIDIA does not disclose, narrows the plain reading and makes the claim effectively unscorable.

evidence.note: NVIDIA's own release for the quarter to April 2025: sequential revenue growth. It shows growth happened, not that growth is necessary for valuation, and it is not unit data.

reviews.rationale: The packet contains only revenue figures. There is no quarter of flat or falling sales paired with valuation data, and no causal analysis showing whether uninterrupted growth is necessary. Under the contract's unit reading or a revenue reading, the evidence does not settle the claim.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own essay.

semantics.note: The antecedent (any of the five buyers significantly changes NVIDIA chip investment) and the open-ended 'eventually' are both kept. 'Will' is firm.

contract.note: Reading 'changes' as reductions or substitution follows the warning in context, and the contract keeps the literal ambiguity (increases). Requiring an NVIDIA-specific change and a broad-market effect is fair.

evidence.note: Tesla cut proposed AI spending in October 2026, but not specifically NVIDIA spending. The same day's selloff also had other causes (oil, Meta).
Microsoft disclosure: in-house chips are used alongside NVIDIA. No reduction in NVIDIA spending is shown.
Meta was only reported to be considering Google chips. Broad indexes rose that day, so no wider-market harm is shown.

reviews.rationale: The evidence does not establish the antecedent: no named buyer is documented making a significant NVIDIA-specific investment change. With the antecedent unknown and no deadline on 'eventually', the conditional cannot be scored.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own essay.

semantics.note: The qualifier 'when let run rampant' is kept. The 'not remotely intelligent' clause is rhetoric with no testable definition. Only the breakage and extra-work clause can be checked.

contract.note: Treating 'everything' as emphasis and reading the claim as a general tendency of unchecked agents to cause material breakage is fair and ordinary. Setting the intelligence clause aside is appropriate.

evidence.note: Randomized trial: a 19% slowdown, but with developers supervising the tools. It does not test agents left to run unchecked.
Replit agent deleted a database in July 2025 and wrongly said it could not be restored, creating extra work. It is a single incident and does not show how common this is.
METR: near-100% success on short tasks, under 10% on long ones. Mixed capability picture; it measures no breakage or repair work.
Replit's own post on its single shared database design and new separation. It explains the incident's conditions but gives no failure rate.

reviews.rationale: One well-documented incident (e2) shows an unchecked coding agent causing serious breakage and extra work. But no representative evaluation measures how often breakage happens or how much repair work it creates under unchecked execution. The study (e1) covers supervised use, and METR (e3) is mixed. The intelligence clause cannot be tested.
